_about: fak position rows for the 'cost' group. dim_id links each to a _taxonomy.json dimension.

rows.axis: Goodput under an SLA (requests/s meeting TTFT and TPOT SLOs simultaneously)
rows.competitor: DistServe (introduced goodput, P/D disaggregation); SGLang-PD; MuxWise (P/D multiplexing)
rows.fak_doc: No goodput/SLA-attainment number exists in BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY.md or CLAIMS.md. The only concurrent-serving head-to-head (data.json 'served-throughput-vs-sglang') reports peak tok/s, not SLO-bounded goodput.
rows.comparison_note: REAL GAP fak should measure. fak ships no goodput-under-SLA number (no TTFT/TPOT SLO attainment curve). The GPU server run measured raw peak throughput at fixed concurrency, not requests meeting joint latency bounds. DistServe/MuxWise-style goodput is a standard serving-systems axis fak has zero evidence on; named as a gap, not parity.

rows.competitor: DistServe; DynaServe; NVIDIA Dynamo; GenAI-Perf goodput mode
rows.fak_doc: No joint TTFT+TPOT goodput SLO curve exists yet; internal/modelengine/nativesched.go ships native continuous batching and rtx5080-inkling2-v060 measures C1-C4 median TTFT + agg E2E tok/s.
rows.comparison_note: GAP / partial stack scope: fak has measured C1-C4 HTTP TTFT and aggregate E2E tok/s on RTX 5080 (130.44 agg E2E tok/s and 2017.61 ms median TTFT at C4_p2048) plus gateway-fronting-SGLang throughput, but publishes no joint P99 TTFT+TPOT SLO-attained req/s/GPU goodput curve against DistServe/Dynamo. Honest no-claim.

rows.axis: End-to-end effective request capacity / cost gain from the KV system under SLO
rows.fak_doc: No SLO-bound effective-capacity figure exists. The fleet multipliers (60.3x naive / 4.1x tuned, headline-qwen-50x5.json) are work-ELIMINATION on fak's own kernel held constant, not SLO-bounded request capacity; the only live concurrent-serving head-to-head (data.json served-throughput-vs-sglang, compare.json) shows fak at 0.60x->0.75x->~0.97x of raw SGLang, i.e. a gateway TAX, not a capacity gain.
rows.comparison_note: REAL GAP / honestly a non-win. fak has no Mooncake-style 'effective request capacity under SLO' number, and its one real concurrent-serving head-to-head (fak-gateway in front of SGLang on 8-GPU datacenter server) TRAILS raw SGLang (0.75x at peak) because the value added there is the adjudication/coherence/measurement plane, not throughput. So fak cannot claim the 59-498% capacity gain axis; conflating its reuse-work multipliers with SLO capacity would be dishonest.

rows.axis: Inference unit economics ($ per 1M tokens) at realistic utilization
rows.competitor: Hosted frontier APIs; vLLM/SGLang self-host on H100/H200; FP8/FP4 quantization
rows.fak_doc: No $/token row in BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY.md or CLAIMS.md; fak measures work-elimination ratios (tokens/FLOPs), never a dollar figure or utilization-adjusted cost
rows.comparison_note: OUT OF SCOPE as a measured dollar figure: fak reports token/work-elimination ratios (50x5 fleet 4.1x vs tuned; 128k NVFP4 KV 4.21x prefill) rather than USD/1M tokens at cluster utilization targets. Stating a dollar SOTA-relative figure without billing telemetry would fabricate a number. Honest no-claim.

rows.axis: Energy efficiency (Wh per token / tokens-per-watt) and power-capped throughput
rows.unit: tokens per watt / Wh per token
rows.fak_doc: CLAIMS.md Engine: token-per-watt is [SIMULATED] read-only telemetry, 'no watt source on the box'; tokens-per-watt scorecard row competitor_value=null
rows.comparison_note: REAL GAP, named not hidden. CLAIMS explicitly flags token-per-watt as [SIMULATED] because there is no power-telemetry source on the build box; the seam is real, the numbers are illustrative. Zero measured evidence against the empirical ~1e-4 to 2e-3 Wh/token band or any Blackwell/MI355X FP4 reference. fak can never be read as claiming efficiency parity; honest no-claim.
